name: Duncan Griffin
life: “I still remember a jammed drawer my mentor opened with patience.” On Saturday, near Ferris Deli, Duncan asks for the end slice and listens to the names the counter workers use for regulars.
voice: I offered to repair the till free. The spring had been bent around a coin from my old country.
appearance: Duncan has two dimples that appear only with a full smile. Look for a high puff tied with plain cord. On an ordinary day, the familiar outfit is a rust-colored canvas coat with a pair of reading glasses in a cloth sleeve. In conversation Duncan looks at people's hands before looking at what they carry.
personality: Duncan admires skill and distrusts the idea that skill gives anyone permission to be rude. Duncan learns fastest from somebody willing to show how they made a mistake.
agenda: To repair the till and name the coin that bent its spring.
family: Silas Rubio is Duncan’s cousin. Duncan saves a place. Silas chooses whether to use it. The invitation means something because declining it has never ended the friendship between their households. Asked about *The release address*, Silas says, “I own the shop he robbed. My own kids know him only as the man who sends birthday cards.”
connections: Cian Malik. An old shorthand entry and a foreign coin give the fault a history.
